confidence_note: The old text said twenty weeks and 'most participants'; the published trial (van der Kolk and colleagues, J Clin Psychiatry 2014) had 64 women with chronic, treatment-resistant PTSD, weekly one-hour classes for 10 weeks, yoga versus a women's health education class; 16 of 31 yoga participants no longer met PTSD criteria (about half), versus roughly one in five in the comparison group (comparison figure from memory, state as 'about one in five'). The detail that the book presents this study is likely but the exact wording is not checked.
facts: Van der Kolk and colleagues ran a randomized trial of yoga for women with chronic PTSD that had not responded to treatment.
64 women took part, split between a trauma-sensitive yoga class and a women's health education class.
Both met once a week for an hour over 10 weeks.
By the end, about half of the yoga group no longer met the criteria for PTSD, against about one in five in the education group.
Van der Kolk says yoga helps people notice sensations in their body in a safe setting, which many trauma survivors avoid or fear.
He holds that talking alone changes understanding but does not necessarily settle the body's alarm, so body-based work belongs alongside talk therapy.
scene_details: comparison with a health education class
tension: Years of talk therapy and medication had not helped these women, and then a weekly yoga class did.
opening_idea: Open on the 64 women who had not improved with usual treatments and what they were assigned.

lessons.idea: Understanding something with your mind does not always settle your body, so you may need a practice that works on the body directly.
lessons.anchor: Yoga group versus health education group.

reflect_final: Which physical practice, such as walking, stretching or slow breathing, could you give a regular slot this month to see how your tension changes?

use_cases.situation: A friend says therapy helps them understand but not feel better.
use_cases.move: Mention the yoga trial and suggest trying a gentle body practice alongside talking.

use_cases.situation: Your shoulders are tight at the end of every meeting.
use_cases.move: Put a two-minute breathing pause on the calendar after the longest meeting.

use_cases.situation: You notice a tension that never leaves.
use_cases.move: Note where it sits and when it eases during a slow walk.

pocket_idea: If understanding has not eased the tension, give your body its own weekly hour.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A weekly yoga class helped women whom talk and pills had not reached.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Van der Kolk's team gave 64 women with stubborn PTSD either yoga or health education for 10 weekly classes. By the end about half of the yoga group no longer met PTSD criteria, compared with about one in five in the other group.
conversation_variants.question_idea: What does your body need that talking has not given it?
